reason: The cited evidence supports the general capability of active-learning ML potentials to capture diverse configurations (E1, E3) and their applicability to solid/liquid simulations (E2, E3), but no evidence is provided for CoCrFeNiMn specifically, for quantitative reduction in TI mismatch, or for improved phase-space overlap over EAM in this context. The key premises thus remain largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Active-learning ML potentials can be trained iteratively on AIMD data to capture diverse atomic configurations of high-entropy alloys near melting.
ML potentials trained this way will represent the ab initio liquid state more accurately than traditional EAM models.
Improved configurational representation will increase phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems in thermodynamic integration.
Increased phase-space overlap will significantly reduce the free-energy mismatch in TI compared to EAM references.
The approach is applicable to equimolar CoCrFeNiMn in both solid and liquid phases near 0.9–1.1 Tm.
